title: The Truth About Organic Food (I Believed the Wrong Thing for Years)
summary: A dietitian weighs organic pros and cons and explains why she switched, citing lower residues, pesticide regulation gaps and vulnerable groups.

assertions.quote: organic it doesn't mean that it is pesticide-free entirely
there is significantly lower pesticide residues found on organic produce compared to the conventional farmed equivalents
more antioxidants in some of the foods like polyphenols and vitamin C
organic food can actually have a higher risk of mycotoxins

verdicts.note: Reviews of organic and conventional cereals find similar or lower mycotoxin levels in organic grain.
A meta-analysis found lower deoxynivalenol contamination in organic cereals and no difference for ochratoxin A.

assertions.quote: in some cases the levels drop by over 80% after just one week of eating organic
less pesticide equals lower risk exposure, which equals better long-term odds
certain groups in particular, like kids and pregnant women, may be especially vulnerable to low-dose pesticide effects
neither system, US or Australia, mandates assessment of combined long-term low-dose exposure to multiple chemicals across the diet
They do also tend to have better levels of omega-3 in them
there have been a number of fraudulent cases, at least in America, where they have found to have not actually been producing organic produce
you are still better off eating conventionally farmed fruit and vegetables than not eating these foods at all
